core.title: Prefix each plan-artifact step sequence with one of the nine step codes
core.given: A plan artifact's step-code sequence prefix (in its URN and its file name) is being selected, changed, or evaluated.
core.when: The planner chooses or checks the single-letter step code that prefixes the plan artifact's step sequence.
core.then: Use exactly one code from D L P C E M Y R K, the one whose step intent matches the plan-artifact step: D define (requirements, criteria, constraints), L locate (discover/find resources), P prepare (setup/configure prerequisites), C confirm (verify/validate conditions), E execute (perform/run the main action), M monitor (observe/track progress), Y modify (update/adjust state), R resolve (fix/handle issues), K conclude (complete/finalize).
prefer: Pick the letter by the step's intent from the code table, not by the first letter of the verb (modify is Y, conclude is K).
Use the same code consistently in the plan artifact's URN and its file name.
avoid: Inventing letters or multi-letter codes outside the nine-code vocabulary.
Choosing a code by spelling (e.g. M for modify, C for conclude) instead of by the defined mapping.
Defaulting every plan-artifact step to E to avoid deciding the step's intent.
core.why: Plan-artifact URNs and file names embed the step code, so a closed, shared letter→intent vocabulary keeps plan-artifact identifiers parseable and the step's purpose readable from its id.
evidence: Every plan-artifact URN/file-name step-code prefix is a member of {D, L, P, C, E, M, Y, R, K}.
Reviewer confirms the chosen letter's intent (per the code table) matches what the plan-artifact step does, including for existing plan artifacts whose body was edited.
verification: Mechanical check on identifiers: every plan-artifact URN and file name carries exactly one step-code letter from the closed set {D, L, P, C, E, M, Y, R, K}; a single uppercase letter is required, and anything else (unknown letter, multi-letter code) is a finding.

Judged check: whether the chosen letter's intent matches what the step does is not mechanically checkable and is judged against the code table's intent glosses — D define requirements, criteria, or constraints; L locate, discover, or find resources; P prepare, setup, or configure prerequisites; C confirm, verify, or validate conditions; E execute, perform, or run the main action; M monitor, observe, or track progress; Y modify, update, or adjust state; R resolve, fix, or handle issues; K conclude, complete, or finalize — including re-judging existing plan artifacts whose body edits changed the step's intent. The mechanical check does not cover this intent match.

values: step-code prefix outside the closed nine-code vocabulary
step-code letter does not match the step's intent

fires: The planner authors a new plan artifact and must pick its step-code prefix for the URN/file name.
The planner renames or re-sequences an existing plan artifact.
The planner edits a plan artifact's body so that the step's intent changes, making the existing prefix potentially wrong.
Planner or reviewer evaluates an existing plan artifact whose prefix is a valid letter but does not match the step's intent.
A plan artifact's URN or file name uses a prefix letter outside D L P C E M Y R K.
doesNotFire: Editing plan-artifact body text (wording, examples) without changing the step's intent and without touching its URN, file name or step code.
Authoring wagons (bounded product slices), acceptances or docs that neither name nor imply a plan-artifact sequence prefix.
Coder or tester work on implementation files that do not name plan artifacts.

neutralityNotes: This convention is planning-method level and almost entirely neutral: no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path is named. The only neutralization is 'WMBT' → the plan-artifact role, split across two profile keys: roles.plan_artifact.name carries the local name used in prose and task terms ('WMBT'), and roles.plan_artifact.kinds carries the concrete step-coded artifact kind matched by the file_kind fact ('wmbt'). The nine-code letter→intent vocabulary (D L P C E M Y R K) is the convention's own content and ATDD-method vocabulary shared across stacks, so it stays in the core. 'URN' and 'file name' are kept as generic identifier surfaces; bun.json names no concrete shape for them. 'Wagon' is method vocabulary (a bounded product slice) and is kept. Term-registry and finding ids remain Bun realization details.
